title: Hello & Hi
topic_brief: The doorway greetings — salaam alaykum, ahlan, and the family's warm reply — because the first three seconds at the threshold set whether you read as a guest or as family.

title: How are you?
topic_brief: Asking izzayak/izzayik and answering el-hamdulillah, since Egyptian greeting is a back-and-forth ritual, not a single line, and returning the question shows you care.

title: Please & Thanks
topic_brief: Law samaht, shukran, and the essential reply mercies (mutashakkir, ma'a salama energy) that keep you polite through every small handover of the day.

title: At the Door: Blessings & Being Welcomed In
topic_brief: The doorstep exchange beyond hello — asking permission to enter, praising the home, and answering the flood of 'ahlan wa sahlan / itfaddal' with the right word so you cross the threshold gracefully instead of frozen.

title: Introductions: Names, Titles & Who's Who
topic_brief: Saying your own name, learning theirs, and above all using the respect titles for mother, father, aunt, uncle and elder siblings — because calling his mother 'Tante' instead of her first name is the single fastest way to be liked.

title: Tea, Juice & the Art of Refusing Then Accepting
topic_brief: The food-and-drink dance: the polite first refusal, the insistence you'll receive, and the warm yes that follows — plus how to praise the food and stop the fourth helping without offending the cook.

title: Telling Them About Yourself
topic_brief: Short, confident lines about where you're from, your work, your family and how long you're staying, so the inevitable spotlight moment feels like sharing rather than an interrogation.

title: Compliments That Land
topic_brief: Praising the home, the cooking, the children and the family's kindness, with the God-willing phrases (ma sha' Allah, tislam eedeek) that make a compliment sound sincere and culturally correct instead of flat.

title: The Questions They'll Ask You
topic_brief: Recognizing and answering the questions that always come — do you like Egypt, can you eat spicy food, will you learn Arabic, when's the wedding — so you can respond with warmth and a little humor instead of a blank stare.

title: When You're Lost: Asking for Slower, Simpler, Again
topic_brief: Graceful survival tools for the moment the room speeds past you — asking them to repeat or slow down, admitting you didn't understand, and asking your partner to translate without breaking the mood.

title: If You Mess Up: Apologizing & Laughing It Off
topic_brief: Recovering from a wrong word, a refused plate or an accidental rudeness with sorry-I'm-still-learning phrases and self-deprecating humor, because how you handle the stumble is what they'll actually remember.

title: Leaving Well: Goodbyes, Thanks & See You Again
topic_brief: The long Egyptian farewell — thanking the hosts properly, promising to return, blessings for the household and the final ma'a salama — so the day closes on affection and an open door rather than an awkward exit.
